finding.rationale: Enumeration of Conditional Access policies via GET /identity/conditionalAccess/policies exposes the defender's detection coverage and policy gaps to an adversary — revealing which user populations lack MFA, which locations are trusted, and which applications have no CA coverage. The control is the set of directory roles that can read CA policies through Microsoft Graph: Security Reader, Security Administrator, Global Reader, Conditional Access Administrator, and Global Secure Access Administrator (Policy.Read.All, per the Microsoft Graph 'List policies' reference). Keep assignments to these roles to the accounts whose job needs them, prefer PIM-eligible over active assignment, and give accounts that only need audit or usage reports Reports Reader, which cannot read CA policies. Severity re-triaged medium -> high (2026-09-10) per docs/finding-severity-rubric-v0.1.md v1.0: the defensive-evasion escalator was adopted — a defender's-own-detection map (CA-policy posture; D=2 sub-case (b)) routes to high. Original point-in-time assessment was medium; preserved here for context. Control corrected 2026-10-12: this record previously named Reports Reader as the control, but Reports Reader is not a supported role for reading CA policies. mapping_id and filename are kept unchanged so the R011-R015 triage records that reference them still resolve.

control.control_id: CA policy read roles (Security Reader, Global Reader, Conditional Access Administrator)
